architecture.graph.title: MalouChat Architecture
architecture.graph.description: Explore MalouChat's product capabilities and architecture, from user-facing AI workflows to the frontend, backend, storage, and external AI services.
architecture.graph.layers.product.label: Product layer
architecture.graph.layers.product.description: User-facing workflows: authentication, conversation management, AI chat, attachments, memories, knowledge base collaboration, preferences, and model administration.
architecture.graph.layers.technical.label: Implementation layer
architecture.graph.layers.technical.description: Engineering foundations: frontend, backend APIs, runtime model configuration, AI orchestration, RAG, databases, object storage, external models, and deployment.
architecture.graph.groups.product.label: User-facing capabilities
architecture.graph.groups.frontend.label: Frontend
architecture.graph.groups.backend.label: Backend
architecture.graph.groups.external.label: External systems
architecture.graph.nodes.product-entry.label: Sign in / Register
architecture.graph.nodes.product-entry.summary: Users can register, sign in, or return as a guest and restore their AI workspace.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-entry.details: Sign-in and registration share one page with a guest option. Guests use the same token lifetimes as registered users. Database-generated names and high-entropy browser recovery keys restore guest identity after session expiration. Route guards redirect unauthenticated users; Zustand, stored tokens, and guest identity restore sessions.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-chat.label: AI chat workspace
architecture.graph.nodes.product-chat.summary: Ask follow-up questions in a conversation and receive AI responses as they stream.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-chat.details: The chat workspace provides conversation, knowledge base, and memory navigation on the left, messages and reasoning in the center, and a composer for text, attachments, knowledge references, voice input, and sending controls below.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-conversation-managem: Organize conversations into projects, create, pin, rename, delete, and switch between previous conversations.

The sidebar separates projects from general conversations. Projects have an icon, color, title, and ongoing instructions that enter each conversation's system prompt. Each conversation belongs to at most one project. Drag-and-drop and menus move conversations into, between, or out of projects.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-message-operations.s: Edit, copy, delete, and regenerate messages, and inspect reasoning.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-message-operations.d: Individual messages support copying, editing, deletion, and regeneration. AI responses stream in real time, reasoning appears in collapsible sections, and generation state can be restored after disconnection.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-ai-capabilities.summ: The assistant can search the web, generate images, understand location, and use contextual tools.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-ai-capabilities.deta: Real-time questions can trigger web search, drawing requests can generate images, and local questions can use browser location and Amap. Responses can also draw on attachments, knowledge bases, memories, and response style preferences.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-files.label: Attachment understanding
architecture.graph.nodes.product-files.summary: Upload files or images for the AI to analyze in the current message.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-files.details: Supports text, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, images, and other attachments. Small text enters the context directly, large text uses semantic search, and images receive multimodal analysis.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory.label: Long-term memory management
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory.summary: Manage personal memories while the AI extracts useful information from conversations.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory.details: Memories help the AI understand profiles, preferences, facts, and summaries over time. Users can manage memories, and the backend determines whether information should be remembered after a response.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-preferences.label: Personal settings
architecture.graph.nodes.product-preferences.summary: Adjust the theme, default model, and response style.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-preferences.details: The settings dialog contains theme selection, model preferences, response style, and sign-out. Model and style preferences affect later responses without changing conversation history.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-model-admin.label: Model administration
architecture.graph.nodes.product-model-admin.summary: Administrators manage selectable models and specialized AI capabilities centrally instead of relying on hardcoded settings.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-model-admin.details: The /admin page manages chat, embedding, vision, speech, and image models. Chat models support multiple configurations, a default, drag ordering, and switching all users. Each specialized capability has one active configuration; image settings include size, prompt enhancement, and watermarking.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-management: Manage knowledge base content, attachments, processing status, and visibility on a dedicated page.

Knowledge bases are independent of conversations. Registered owners can create, upload TXT/DOCX files, edit, replace attachments, delete, and switch private/team visibility while reviewing processing status. Guests are prompted to register or sign in before creating one.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-collaborat: Team knowledge bases support invitations, accepting or declining, membership management, and leaving.
Owners invite, manage, and remove members. Invited users accept or decline after signing in. Members can reference a knowledge base or leave it, but cannot update or delete it.
Select an accessible knowledge base in chat to ground answers in your own material.

Knowledge bases can be linked from the composer. Access and processing status are checked before sending. If membership is removed or visibility becomes private, the unavailable reference is cleared and a helpful message is shown.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-project-context.summ: Organize conversations by project and apply consistent project instructions.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-project-context.deta: A project contains multiple conversations with a shared icon, color, title, and ongoing instructions. Instructions enter the model context for every conversation in the project.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-conversation-movemen: Organize conversations across projects and the general list using drag-and-drop or menus.
Move general conversations into projects, between projects, or back to the general list. Changes are persisted by the backend; moving to the same location does not issue a request.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-conversation-find.su: Highlight frequent conversations and find items in a growing history.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-conversation-find.de: Pin important conversations, search history by keyword, and navigate to matching content. Rename and delete actions remain in the conversation menu.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-message-regenerate.s: Edit an earlier question and regenerate subsequent responses from that point.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-message-regenerate.d: Editing a message truncates the later context and regenerates from the revised question, keeping old and new branches from mixing.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-stream-recovery.summ: Display responses in real time and restore generation state and content after disconnection.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-stream-recovery.deta: Streaming events append AI responses. After an unexpected disconnect, the frontend can resubscribe to a task and restore existing content, reasoning state, and subsequent output.
Analyze visual content and text in images using the current question.
Uploads receive a general visual description; sending can trigger a question-specific analysis. If analysis fails, the model is still informed that an image is attached.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-large-file-qa.label: Semantic questions over large files
architecture.graph.nodes.product-large-file-qa.summar: Choose direct context or semantic retrieval based on file size and locate relevant information.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-large-file-qa.detail: Small text enters the current context directly. Large files are chunked and indexed in the background so the AI can retrieve relevant passages rather than reading only the beginning.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory-extraction.su: Identify and save user information worth keeping across conversations.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory-extraction.de: After a response, the system evaluates whether information should be remembered and extracts profiles, preferences, facts, and summaries. Temporary information is skipped.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory-control.label: User-controlled management
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory-control.summa: Review and correct personal information retained by the AI.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-memory-control.detai: The memory page provides transparent control over retained information, including review, editing, and deletion.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-web-search.label: Web search
architecture.graph.nodes.product-web-search.summary: The AI searches the web when questions require current information.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-web-search.details: The model uses web search for recent facts, news, and live information, then integrates the results into its answer. Users do not need a separate search mode.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-image-generation.sum: Generate images from natural-language descriptions and display them in conversations.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-image-generation.det: Drawing requests trigger image generation. Results are copied to object storage and returned as image messages with preview and download actions.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-location-awareness.s: With permission, use current location to answer weather, nearby, and local questions.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-location-awareness.d: The AI requests browser location permission and converts coordinates into a readable region. Location is used only within that tool call, without frontend keyword-triggered collection.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-model-style.label: Models and response style
architecture.graph.nodes.product-model-style.summary: Persist model and tone preferences for a consistent personal experience.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-model-style.details: Choose a default model, response style, and theme. Model and style preferences affect later responses without rewriting history.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-chat-model-governanc: Control selectable models, their default and order, and switch all users when needed.
Administrators add chat models, select a default, and drag to reorder. User settings follow the same order. When a model expires or its quota fails, all users can be switched to another model.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-specialized-model-go: Configure one active model for embeddings, vision, speech, and image generation.

Each specialized capability has separate settings. Speech transcription uses an OpenAI-compatible or DashScope-native interface depending on the model family. Image generation additionally stores size, prompt enhancement, and watermark settings.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-stable-upd: Edit content or replace files without changing identity or existing references.
Owners can change the title, content, or attachment while retaining the knowledge base ID, memberships, and conversation references.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-reindex.su: Rechunk and reindex changed content and show processing progress.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-reindex.de: Content or attachment changes enqueue processing again for chunking and vector indexing. Completion, processing, and failure icons communicate status.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-visibility: Owners choose whether knowledge is personal or shared with invited members.
Private and team visibility changes require confirmation. Switching back to private removes all members and revokes their access.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-invitation-lifecycle: Search users, invite in bulk, and handle acceptance or rejection.
Owners search by username or email and select users to invite. Invitees see pending invitations after sign-in, join on acceptance, or dismiss them by declining.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-roles.summ: Owners manage content and membership; members can reference the knowledge base or leave.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-roles.deta: Owners can update, delete, invite, and remove members. Members cannot change content or the team and can only reference the knowledge base or leave.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-membership-exit.summ: Owners can remove members, and members can end their participation.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-membership-exit.deta: Removal or leaving deletes membership immediately. The backend also clears the user's conversation bindings to that knowledge base.
Check knowledge base access before a request enters generation.
Access validation prevents unavailable knowledge base references from entering generation and rolls back the temporary user message on rejection.
architecture.graph.nodes.product-knowledge-revocation: Existing references become unavailable after removal or switching to private.
The backend clears affected conversation bindings. Pre-send and streaming validation prevent further use even before a page refresh.
Combine semantic relevance and keyword matches for long documents and short queries.
Knowledge questions combine vector retrieval, keyword supplementation, and full-source recovery for older indexes, covering more than document beginnings and supporting short names and terms.
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-app.label: React frontend
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-app.summary: React 19, Vite, Zustand, and Ant Design form the user experience layer.
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-app.details: The frontend handles routing, session restoration, chat layout, knowledge bases, model administration, settings, architecture views, mobile layouts, and streaming messages.
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-model-admin.label: Model management frontend
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-model-admin.summary: A responsive /admin page provides model configuration, ordering, and bulk switching.
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-model-admin.details: AdminView uses the shared sidebar for chat and specialized model sections. Sortable manages chat model ordering. Writes use administrator APIs through admin-model and work on desktop and mobile.
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-network.label: Frontend communication layer
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-network.summary: Shared HTTP, SSE, tokens, file URLs, and client tool result handling.
architecture.graph.nodes.frontend-network.details: The API layer handles authentication, 401 responses, guest identity restoration, SSE parsing, upload progress, temporary file URLs, browser capability execution, and result submission.
architecture.graph.nodes.browser-client-tools.label: Browser capability executor
architecture.graph.nodes.browser-client-tools.summary: Execute browser capabilities requested by the backend and return results to the tool workflow.
architecture.graph.nodes.browser-client-tools.details: The backend sends client-tool-request over SSE. The frontend calls web/src/utils/client-tools.ts; getBrowserLocation uses navigator.geolocation, then POSTs client-tool-result to resume the backend tool.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-api.summary: Backend APIs under /api provide authentication, conversations, messages, files, memories, knowledge bases, and model administration.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-api.details: Express modules separate controllers, services, routes, and schemas. Middleware handles authentication, validation, and errors. Authentication supports registered and recoverable guest identities; Prisma accesses the database.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-guest-auth.label: Recoverable guest authentication
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-guest-auth.summary: Generate sequential guest names and recover browser identities using high-entropy keys.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-guest-auth.details: POST /api/auth/guest hashes recovery keys with SHA-256 to find returning guests. New guests receive a Visitor_0001-style name from an atomic PostgreSQL sequence. Guests and registered users share JWT and refresh cookie lifetimes.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-model-management.sum: Administrator-only model CRUD, ordering, and bulk preference updates.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-model-management.det: The admin-models module validates settings, enforces defaults, reorders models, switches all users, and invalidates runtime caches. Administrator middleware restricts access.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-knowledge.label: Knowledge base access service
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-knowledge.summary: Knowledge base CRUD, editing, invitations, members, and conversation access.
architecture.graph.nodes.backend-knowledge.details: The backend enforces private/team access and invitation and membership actions. messages/stream validates access before persistence; permission changes clear conversation bindings.
architecture.graph.nodes.ai-orchestrator.label: AI orchestration
architecture.graph.nodes.ai-orchestrator.summary: LangChain model calls, tool loops, deep thinking, and context assembly.
architecture.graph.nodes.ai-orchestrator.details: Combines conversation history, memories, files, knowledge bases, response style, and tools into model calls. Supports reasoning_content and multi-round tool calling.
architecture.graph.nodes.ai-model-registry.label: Runtime model registry
architecture.graph.nodes.ai-model-registry.summary: Read active model settings from the database and provide unified configuration with a short-lived cache.
architecture.graph.nodes.ai-model-registry.details: model-registry reads AiModel by type for selectable chat models, specialized defaults, and image parameters. Writes invalidate caches immediately; safe built-in fallbacks keep core AI capabilities available during database outages.
architecture.graph.nodes.rag-system.label: RAG retrieval system
architecture.graph.nodes.rag-system.summary: Text chunking, embeddings, pgvector retrieval, TopK supplementation, and keyword fallback.
architecture.graph.nodes.rag-system.details: Files and knowledge bases are split into overlapping chunks and embedded into pgvector. Relevant passages enter prompts; short-name queries also use keyword fallback.
architecture.graph.nodes.tool-runtime.label: Tools and browser bridge
architecture.graph.nodes.tool-runtime.summary: Shared runtime for webSearch, drawImage, readFile, semanticSearch, and location tools.
architecture.graph.nodes.tool-runtime.details: Request-scoped context enforces access. webSearchTool connects to DashScope WebSearch MCP, drawImageTool generates and copies images to R2, and getUserLocationTool combines browser coordinates with Amap reverse geocoding.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-database.summary: Neon PostgreSQL stores business data; pgvector supports vector search.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-database.details: The database stores user types, guest key hashes, visitor sequences, conversations, messages, memories, files, knowledge bases, memberships, invitations, AiModel settings, and chunk vectors. The Prisma schema defines the data model.
architecture.graph.nodes.data-ai-model-config.label: AiModel configuration table
architecture.graph.nodes.data-ai-model-config.summary: Persist unified settings for chat, embedding, vision, speech, and image models.
architecture.graph.nodes.data-ai-model-config.details: AiModel stores identifiers, display names, types, defaults, selectability, ordering, dimensions, and JSON parameters. Chat models allow multiple entries; specialized capabilities use the configured default.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-storage.summary: Object storage for attachments, images, and generated results.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-storage.details: Business interfaces store storageKey. The frontend resolves signed URLs in batches. Image generation and uploads share R2 storage.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-dashscope-websearch: DashScope WebSearch MCP provides live web retrieval for webSearchTool.
server/src/lib/tools/webSearch.ts initializes MyMcpClient with DASHSCOPE_WEBSEARCH_MCP_URL and DASHSCOPE_API_KEY, then calls bailian_web_search to supply current information to the model.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-dashscope-image.sum: The DashScope image endpoint generates images for drawImageTool.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-dashscope-image.det: server/src/lib/tools/drawImage.ts uses DASHSCOPE_IMAGE_GENERATION_URL and administrator model settings. AiModel supplies the model, size, prompt enhancement, and watermark. Temporary results are downloaded and copied to Cloudflare R2.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-amap.label: Amap reverse geocoding
architecture.graph.nodes.external-amap.summary: Amap converts browser coordinates into readable administrative regions.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-amap.details: getUserLocationTool requests getBrowserLocation, then calls Amap with AMAP_REGEOCODE_URL and AMAP_API_KEY to return country, province, city, and district to the model.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-ai.label: DashScope LLM / Embeddings
architecture.graph.nodes.external-ai.summary: DashScope / OpenAI-compatible models, embeddings, and multimodal analysis.
architecture.graph.nodes.external-ai.details: Model services provide chat, reasoning_content, embeddings, and vision analysis. Web search, image generation, and location appear as separate external nodes to clarify tool boundaries.
architecture.graph.nodes.deployment.label: Deployment and reverse proxy
architecture.graph.nodes.deployment.summary: Docker, Nginx, two Railway services, and health checks.
architecture.graph.nodes.deployment.details: server and web deploy independently. Nginx serves frontend assets and proxies /api and /health to the backend.
architecture.graph.edges.0.label: Enter workspace
architecture.graph.edges.1.label: Manage conversations
architecture.graph.edges.2.label: Message actions

architecture.graph.flows.product-chat-flow.label: AI chat product workflow
architecture.graph.flows.product-chat-flow.descriptio: After sign-in, users organize and find conversations, then combine message actions, attachments, memories, preferences, and AI capabilities to complete tasks.
architecture.graph.flows.product-knowledge-flow.label: Knowledge base product workflow
architecture.graph.flows.product-knowledge-flow.descr: Knowledge bases are uploaded, edited, reindexed, and shared on a dedicated page before being referenced in chat. They are independently maintained knowledge assets.
architecture.graph.flows.product-model-admin-flow.des: Administrators maintain chat and specialized models. Defaults and ordering appear in user settings; bulk switching and current specialized configurations are available when needed.
architecture.graph.flows.model-management-technical-f: Administrator APIs persist AiModel settings and invalidate caches. Chat, RAG, vision, speech, and image calls resolve current settings through the runtime registry before using external services.
architecture.graph.flows.guest-auth-technical-flow.de: The frontend reads a stored recovery key and calls guest authentication. The backend finds the hashed key or creates a sequential guest name, then returns a standard JWT session.
architecture.graph.flows.chat-technical-flow.label: AI chat implementation flow
architecture.graph.flows.chat-technical-flow.descript: The frontend connects to message services through API/SSE. The backend assembles context, invokes tools and models, and streams results back.
architecture.graph.flows.tool-external-flow.label: Tools and external service flow
architecture.graph.flows.tool-external-flow.descripti: Tool execution connects to DashScope search and images, browser location, and Amap. Generated images are stored in R2 before returning to the frontend.
architecture.graph.flows.knowledge-technical-flow.des: Knowledge base services manage access and content. RAG handles chunking, embeddings, storage, and retrieval, injecting relevant passages into model context.
architecture.graph.flows.storage-deploy-flow.label: External systems and deployment flow
architecture.graph.flows.storage-deploy-flow.descript: Prisma accesses PostgreSQL/pgvector and R2 stores objects. Docker, Railway, and Nginx compose the production deployment.
